transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM); Marcus (Novum CTO), Priya (Head of Security), Elliot (ML Eng), Jared (Product)

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. run through an agenda — quick results from last week's run, audit log and SSO questions, retention defaults, then open items.
[00:12] Marcus: Yep thanks, we only have half an hour but hopefully can get clarity.
[00:18] Diego: I can start with the perf summary — we ran the canary suite for 12 hours on the hosted endpoint, average p50 token latency was in the 130 to 160 ms range for 256 token prompts, p95 spiked to ~420ms under the small burst scenario. note this was on the smallest plan because this was a hosted run not dedicated.
[00:42] Elliot: Quick ques — were KV cache warm? We saw different numbers locally when cache warmed.
[00:47] Diego: Good catch. For the run we had a cold KV cache for first hour, then warmed. The numbers I quoted are post-warm. Cold ramp added about 200ms to p95.
[01:05] Jared: That aligns with what we expect. Our main Q is tradeoff — if we go dedicated, can we get token latency down by 30% without exploding costs?
[01:13] Aisha: Short answer yes, Dedicated with reserved capacity + the quantization profile we recommended should get you close. We'll include cost delta in the addendum.
[01:23] Priya: Sorry to jump in — technical perf is great but my priority is compliance. We went through your security pack but need specifics on SSO, audit logs, and retention for the pilot. Also SOC 2 readiness questions.
[01:38] Lina: Absolutely, we prepared a separate section in the pack — Diego, do you want to walk the audit log example?
[01:44] Diego: Sure. So audit logging is available in both Hosted and Dedicated. Example events: request start, model selected, token counts, user_id (obfuscated if requested), request metadata, error codes, and routing decisions. We emit JSON lines to the customer-controlled S3 for Dedicated; for Hosted we can stream to their S3 or to a Splunk/Datadog endpoint via secured forwarder.
[02:06] Priya: When you say user_id obfuscated, can we redact PII by default before logs are stored? We need a policy where any user-identifying fields are hashed or redacted before persistence.
[02:19] Diego: We have a pre-storage redaction hook — currently it's configurable at the tenant level. For Hosted it's off by default for performance but we can enable a pre-send lambda to mask fields; for Dedicated you control the hook. There may be a perf hit but we can quantify.
[02:37] Marcus: Is there an audit-log schema sample? For our compliance team we need sample lines.
[02:42] Diego: Yes — I'll upload a sample export with a 24-hour slice. It includes event_type, timestamp, request_id, model_variant, response_status, token_counts, route, and a hashed user_id.
[02:54] Priya: Good. Also, retention — what's the retention matrix? We need options: 30, 90, 365, or custom. Is retention enforced automatically or do we need to run deletion jobs?
[03:06] Diego: We support retention TTL for logs and KV cache. For Hosted, retention policies are configurable via the Console and we will enforce deletion at object store level. For Dedicated, you can set S3 lifecycle rules on your bucket. For short term POC we can set 30 days by default.
[03:21] Priya: Is there proof-of-deletion or an audit trail when we purge data?
[03:26] Diego: We emit deletion events into the audit log, including what objects were removed and a checksum. For Hosted we provide a signed deletion manifest. For Dedicated you manage deletion but we can run a verification job and sign off.
[03:40] Elliot: On encryption — we prefer customer-managed KMS for Dedicated. Can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS and rotate keys?
[03:48] Diego: Yes, Dedicated supports AWS KMS and GCP KMS; key rotation is supported. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS; CC3 customers can request a bring-your-own-key flow.
[04:02] Priya: SOC 2 — are you SOC 2 Type II? What's the scoping and evidence we can see during the pilot?
[04:08] Aisha: Redwood is in the process — we have SOC 2 Type II for core infra, but some newer services have a scoped roadmap. We'll share the SOC 2 summary and our control matrix. For pilot evidence, we can provide SSOC3? sorry, I'll rephrase — we'll provide the SOC 2 summary report redacted, the control matrix, and we can schedule a scoping call with our security lead.
[04:31] Priya: Ok, we'll want the control matrix and a list of third parties. Also runtime access: can our auditors access logs?
[04:40] Lina: We typically provide auditor access via a time-limited, read-only role or we can create an export bundle. We'll coordinate with your audit contact.
[04:51] Marcus: On SSO — we already use Okta and require SAML + SCIM provisioning. Can Redwood integrate?
[04:59] Diego: Yes — SAML SSO is supported for Console access; SCIM provisioning for user sync is available on enterprise plans. For Dedicated we can do SAML with fine-grained RBAC.
[05:12] Priya: We need to map roles to least privilege — devs shouldn't have access to raw PII, ops needs runbook access, security needs audit logs.
[05:21] Diego: We support RBAC roles: Admin, Operator, Developer, Auditor. We can create a custom Auditor role that only sees audit exports and not payloads.
[05:33] Jared: Quick perf follow-up — if we enable pre-storage redaction, how much perf hit? Diego you mentioned quantification?
[05:40] Diego: Ballpark from previous POCs: pre-storage redaction lambda added 15–40ms per request on average, depending on complexity of redaction and whether it's inline. If you need full payload scrubbing before hitting disk it can go higher; alternate pattern is to store encrypted payloads and scrub asynchronously.
[06:00] Priya: For compliance we prefer scrubbing before persistence. Async scrubbing is risky.
[06:06] Elliot: We can prototype scrubbing logic in our canary dataset so we know the perf impact.
[06:10] Aisha: Great — so action item: Diego will share audit log sample and a demo script, Elliot will push the canary dataset, Priya to confirm retention/hands-off options, Aisha to send pricing and SOC 2 artifacts.
[06:24] Marcus: Also to note — competitors. We did a side-by-side with Anthropic and some in-house endpoints; latency numbers were similar but we found Redwood's routing and fallback logic preferable for multi-region constraints.
[06:36] Diego: On fallback — we can route to lower-cost regional variants and attach a fallback policy to keep high availability. That will appear in the audit logs as a routing_decision event.
[06:47] Priya: One more — data residency. For POC we need EU region only for EU users. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[06:55] Lina: Yes, for Hosted we can pin to eu-west region; Dedicated obviously in your VPC. We'll document how nested services (logging forwarders, metrics) remain in-region.
[07:08] Jared: Any blockers for us to go to the next phase? From product side, we need to validate: 1) no PII leakage in logs, 2) acceptable latency with scrubbing, 3) cost estimate for dedicated.
[07:20] Aisha: Sounds good. We'll deliver the pack and pricing by Friday and set SOC 2 scoping call for next Tuesday 10am PT.
[07:28] Priya: Works for me.
[07:30] Marcus: Same.
[07:33] Aisha: Cool thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links.

References shared during call:
- Security pack (link): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/novum
- Benchmark instructions: https://redwood.example.com/poc-benchmarks
- Sample audit log (to be uploaded): will appear in the drive link we share

End of transcript.
